restrictions: Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 (C = 2728); total work over all processors. N = 0.994841*2^128 uniform 55-byte single-block messages, each hashed to its full 256-bit reduced r38 digest (standard IV, indices 0..37, feed-forward) by the counted 7-lane 36-bit-guard SWAR batch (2879 charged operations per 7 trials, peak liveness 53 within register-machine-64), asserted by the replay. A 140-bit digest key probes an uninitialised table (six ordinary operations plus the key relabelling and cap test per trial); false 140-bit matches and resampled inputs are rejected by full recomputation.

Worst-case single-run upper bounds including unsuccessful trials; a deterministic candidate cap V bounds all verification work. The collision-existence term is distribution-free; H1 covers only the uninitialised-table overwrite, garbage and cap tails. No witness, executed search, novelty or improvement over the nominal reference is asserted.

Memory 2^146 bytes (2^140 table words) is a reported metric only. nonuniform_advice is zero: a uniform program of public constants, no precomputed collision. The score beats the organizer nominal scaffold 132 by an explicit counted ledger, not by an epistemic claim against 128.

heuristics.statement: For N = 0.994841*2^128 reduced r38 digests of uniform 55-byte single-block messages in fixed processing order, assume Pr[F2] <= N^3/(6*2^396), E[Y1] <= N^2/2^140 and Var[Y1] <= N^2/2^140, where Y1 counts distinct-digest pairs sharing the 140-bit key and F2 is an intervening overwrite of a colliding pair in the uninitialised table. The collision-existence bound Pr[no output collision] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257) and the repeated-input bound are proved distribution-free and are not part of H1.
heuristics.scope: Uninitialised-table retention and candidate-cap tail for this single-block family. H1 does not establish SHA-256 randomness, the full 256-bit collision law, or implementation equivalence.
heuristics.extrapolation: One organizer python-message-pairs-v1 experiment returns 14-bit masked collisions on 256 seeded trials and self-checks the SWAR counts. A successful scaled trial does not establish the full-scale overwrite, garbage or cap margins.
heuristics.limitations: Unproved full-scale overwrite and moment bounds; the experiment's masked scope is a kernel-and-method demonstration, not a full-scale tail proof.
